title: Block-packed KV cache quantization: FP8/INT8/INT4 with adaptive dequant & fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce peak GPU memory for large-sequence KV caching by exploring block-packed quantization schemes (per-block INT4/INT8 with per-block FP8-like scaling) and an adaptive fallback/dequantization policy to preserve generation quality. This ticket scopes experiments, synthetic and real-inference evaluations, and a conservative rollout plan that enables per-tenant policy toggles.

Hypothesis: Using small block-wise quant (e.g., 64-dimension blocks) with learned scale/zero points reduces memory 3-4x vs FP16 while keeping perplexity/LM-consistency degradation < 2% for typical Redwood workloads. INT4 shows best memory but risks outliers on long contexts; FP8-style 8-bit float with block scaling may hit a sweet spot for fidelity.

Deliverables: experiment harness + config, baseline and stress benchmarks, regression dashboard, fallback policy prototype (per-request quality check + dynamic dequant), a short PRD for runtime integration, and a rollout playbook for Dedicated/Private customers.
metrics_and_success_criteria: token-level perplexity delta <= 2% vs FP16 on heldout eval prompts
retrieval rerank MRR drop <= 1% on quantized KV
peak GPU memory reduction >= 2.5x for 70% of traces
95th percentile latency increase <= 10ms for typical 1-2k token requests
experiment_plan: Implement block-packed quantizer supporting INT4/INT8 and simulated FP8 with per-block exponent/scaling metadata
Add fast dequant kernel prototype in CUDA with fused bias-add support to avoid extra memcpy
Run microbenchmarks: memory usage, throughput, quant/dequant cost across sequence lengths [128,1024,4096,8192]
Evaluate quality: perplexity, generation divergence (tok-F1), and end-to-end retrieval+generate flows
Test edge behavior: near-max context, token-drop patterns, rare-token sensitivity
datasets_and_prompts: OpenWebText subset (5k prompts) for generation fidelity
Redwood internal eval prompts (chat, completion, code) - gated
Long-context stress set (10k token synthetic traces)
observations_to_date: 2026-03-03: Initial block INT8 prototype reduced peak KV memory ~2.6x on 4k contexts; throughput regressed ~6% due to dequant cost; quality delta <1% on short prompts
2026-03-06: INT4 gives ~3.8x memory reduction but has sporadic token-level collapse after ~1500 token recursions on a subset of prompts; correlated with narrow activation distributions
2026-03-08: Simulated FP8 (6-bit mantissa/3-bit exp style) at block granularity shows stable quality with ~2.8x memory reduction and only 3-5% dequant overhead
2026-03-09: Per-block variance-aware scaling (compute scale from running mean/var per block) mitigates INT4 collapse in 70% of failing cases
fallback_and_rollout_plan: Conservative: default to INT8 with per-block FP8 for datasets with high variance
Runtime policy: measure 'block-variance' at write time; if above threshold, mark block as 'high-entropy' and store in INT8/FP16 instead of INT4; low-entropy blocks use INT4
Quality safety net: probe generation on a small prefix (16 tokens) using dequantized values; if divergence > threshold, trigger on-the-fly dequant to FP16 for remaining context
Canary rollout: enable for internal infra first, then opt-in Dedicated customers, then automatic for hosted with monitoring gates
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: INT4 failure modes on rare-token sequences. Mitigation: dynamic block-level tagging + conservative fallback to INT8 or FP16.
Risk: dequant latency kills tail latency. Mitigation: fuse dequant into kernel and add adaptive offloading for cold cache blocks.
Risk: storage/metadata overhead for per-block scale causes diminishing returns. Mitigation: amortize by grouping blocks and storing compact headers.
